sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Re-entering society.
sentences.zh: 重返社会。

sentences.en: How to and why for?
sentences.zh: 如何重返？为何重返？

sentences.en: After many months of COVID restrictions,
sentences.zh: 在经历了数月的疫情限制后，

sentences.en: resuming something like our pre-pandemic lives can feel daunting to many people.
sentences.zh: 恢复到某种类似疫情前的生活状态，对许多人来说可能令人望而生畏。

sentences.en: Late Night TV has picked up on this.
sentences.zh: 深夜电视节目也注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: Stephen Colbert recently ran this spoof educational video.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·科尔伯特最近播出了这段恶搞教育视频。

sentences.en: So you spent a year in isolation, then got jabbed in the arm by a stranger.
sentences.zh: 所以，你独自隔离了一年，然后被一个陌生人在胳膊上扎了一针。

sentences.en: Congratulations!
sentences.zh: 恭喜你！

sentences.en: It's the first step in re-entering society.
sentences.zh: 这是重返社会的第一步。

sentences.en: But before you head back out into the world,
sentences.zh: 但在你重新回到这个世界之前，

sentences.en: you need to remember what it's like to be around what scientists call other people.
sentences.zh: 你需要回想一下，和科学家所说的“其他人”待在一起是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Maybe you'll find yourself wondering what your friends think of you.
sentences.zh: 也许你会开始好奇，你的朋友们是怎么看你的。

sentences.en: Do they still think you're witty?
sentences.zh: 他们还觉得你风趣吗？

sentences.en: Are they bored by your small talk?
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得你的闲聊很无聊吗？

sentences.en: Do you even remember how to make small talk?
sentences.zh: 你还记得怎么进行闲聊吗？

sentences.en: Have I always been awkward in social settings?
sentences.zh: 我一直都在社交场合表现得这么笨拙吗？

sentences.en: Maybe I never enjoyed others that much to begin with?
sentences.zh: 也许我本来就不怎么喜欢和别人待在一起？

sentences.en: Oh God, do I look awkward?
sentences.zh: 天哪，我看起来很尴尬吗？

sentences.en: I feel awkward.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很尴尬。

sentences.en: Can they tell I'm thinking this?
sentences.zh: 他们能看出我在想这些吗？

sentences.en: Do I even have a real personality?
sentences.zh: 我真的有真实的个性吗？

sentences.en: Or am I just a construct of all the media I've consumed in
sentences.zh: 还是说，我只是在完全与世隔绝的状态下，

sentences.en: complete isolation?
sentences.zh: 被我所接触的所有媒体塑造出来的一个产物？

sentences.en: What were things even like before this?
sentences.zh: 在这之前，一切是什么样的？

sentences.en: Because remember, the people around
sentences.zh: 因为请记住，你周围的人，

sentences.en: you might feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 可能也有同样的感觉。

sentences.en: It turns out other people do feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，其他人确实有同样的感觉。

sentences.en: And often in those
sentences.zh: 而且往往在我们担心他们评判我们的那些时刻，

sentences.en: moments when we're worrying about them judging us, they're worrying about us judging them.
sentences.zh: 他们也在担心我们评判他们。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we bring you a favorite episode about the power we exert
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们为您带来一期最受欢迎的节目，探讨我们对他人的影响力，

sentences.en: over others and the perils of living too much inside our own heads.
sentences.zh: 以及活在自己内心世界太久所带来的危险。

sentences.en: Philip Zimbardo grew up poor.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·津巴多在贫困中长大。

sentences.en: I was born in New York City in the South Bronx.
sentences.zh: 我出生在纽约市的南布朗克斯区。

sentences.en: And as he went to school and played in his neighborhood, he noticed something.
sentences.zh: 当他上学并在社区里玩耍时，他注意到了一些事情。

sentences.en: There were lots of ways for kids from poor families to get into trouble.
sentences.zh: 贫困家庭的孩子有很多误入歧途的途径。

sentences.en: One of the things about growing up poor is you're surrounded by evil,
sentences.zh: 在贫困中成长的一点是，你会被“邪恶”包围，

sentences.en: meaning people whose job it is to get good kids to do bad things for money.
sentences.zh: 意思是那些以诱导好孩子为了钱做坏事为职业的人。

sentences.en: And even as a little kid, I was always curious about why some kids got seduced
sentences.zh: 即使在小时候，我也一直很好奇，为什么有些孩子会被诱惑，

sentences.en: and other kids like me were able to resiSt.
sentences.zh: 而像我这样的其他孩子却能够抵御。

sentences.en: Were some kids smarter?
sentences.zh: 是有些孩子更聪明吗？

sentences.en: Tougher?
sentences.zh: 更强硬吗？

sentences.en: Lots of people might draw such conclusions,
sentences.zh: 很多人可能会得出这样的结论，

sentences.en: but from an early age, Phil found himself interested in another explanation.
sentences.zh: 但菲尔从小就对另一种解释感兴趣。

sentences.en: the context in which a good kid would do something bad, the situation.
sentences.zh: 即好孩子做坏事的环境，也就是情境。

sentences.en: At school,
sentences.zh: 在学校，

sentences.en: James Monroe High School, also in the Bronx,
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·门罗高中，也在布朗克斯区，

sentences.en: Phil got close to a classmate who was interested in the same questions.
sentences.zh: 菲尔和一个对同样问题感兴趣的同学走得很近。

sentences.en: And it was a little Jewish kid named Stanley Milgram.
sentences.zh: 那是一个叫斯坦利·米尔格拉姆的犹太小男孩。

sentences.en: We were in the same class.
sentences.zh: 我们在同一个班级。

sentences.en: We sat side by side.
sentences.zh: 我们并排坐着。

sentences.en: He was the smartest kid in the class.
sentences.zh: 他是班里最聪明的孩子。

sentences.en: He won all the medals at graduation,
sentences.zh: 他毕业时拿到了所有的奖章，

sentences.en: so obviously nobody liked him because we were all envious of him.
sentences.zh: 所以显然没人喜欢他，因为我们都嫉妒他。

sentences.en: But he was super smart and super serious.
sentences.zh: 但他超级聪明，也超级严肃。

sentences.en: If you knew anything about psychology, you will know that these teenagers went on to become two
sentences.zh: 如果你了解一点心理学，你就会知道，这两个少年后来成为了历史上

sentences.en: of the most influential psychologists in history.
sentences.zh: 最有影响力的两位心理学家。

sentences.en: Phil became famous for conducting the Stanford
sentences.zh: 菲尔因主持斯坦福监狱实验而闻名，

sentences.en: Prison Experiment, where he turned the university's psychology department into a
sentences.zh: 他把大学的心理学系变成了一个

sentences.en: makeshift prison.
sentences.zh: 临时监狱。

sentences.en: Stanley Milgram made his mark with a study that examined the power of situations
sentences.zh: 斯坦利·米尔格拉姆则凭借一项研究留下了自己的印记，该研究考察了情境的力量，

sentences.en: to seduce good people to do bad things.
sentences.zh: 即诱导好人做坏事的力量。

sentences.en: It involved asking a volunteer to administer
sentences.zh: 实验要求一名志愿者对另一个人进行

sentences.en: a memory test to another person.
sentences.zh: 记忆测试。

sentences.en: If the answers were wrong, the volunteer was told to deliver
sentences.zh: 如果回答错误，志愿者会被告知要给予

sentences.en: a series of electrical shocks as punishment.
sentences.zh: 一系列电击作为惩罚。

sentences.en: The study has invited a great deal of admiration
sentences.zh: 多年来，这项研究既招致了极大的赞赏，

sentences.en: and a great deal of criticism over the years.
sentences.zh: 也招致了极大的批评。

sentences.en: We're going to begin today's show by taking you through this famous experiment.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的节目将从带您了解这个著名的实验开始。

sentences.en: As you listen, pay attention to how you're responding to the scene that unfolds,
sentences.zh: 在收听时，请注意你对所展开场景的反应，

sentences.en: what you think about the different characters, and how you relate to them.
sentences.zh: 你对不同角色的看法，以及你如何与他们产生共鸣。

sentences.en: Once it's done, we're going to talk with a psychologist who realized
sentences.zh: 实验结束后，我们将与一位心理学家交谈，他意识到

sentences.en: that most people overlook something in the experiment.
sentences.zh: 大多数人在实验中忽略了一些东西。

sentences.en: We so often sort of simulate, if I was in that Milgram shock experiment,
sentences.zh: 我们经常会模拟，如果我身处那个米尔格拉姆电击实验中，

sentences.en: what would I do if I was the study participant, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我是实验参与者，我会怎么做，对吧？

sentences.en: Would I actually stand up and go against these directives and say no?
sentences.zh: 我会真的站出来反抗这些指令并说不吗？

sentences.en: But we kind of flipped that idea on its head.
sentences.zh: 但我们把这个想法彻底颠覆了。

sentences.en: Stopping to notice what she noticed can lead us to a vital insight about the mind.
sentences.zh: 停下来观察她所注意到的东西，可以让我们对思维有一个至关重要的洞察。

sentences.en: Stanley Milgram grew up in a world that seemed bent on destroying itself.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利·米尔格拉姆成长在一个似乎一心想要自我毁灭的世界里。

sentences.en: World War II was raging in Europe and Asia, and by the time he was eight, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战在欧洲和亚洲肆虐，到他八岁时，美国

sentences.en: was swept up in the conflict.
sentences.zh: 也被卷入了这场冲突。

sentences.en: We interrupt this broadcast to bring you this important bulletin from the United Press.
sentences.zh: 我们中断广播，为您带来这条来自合众国际社的重要快讯。

sentences.en: The White House announces Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.
sentences.zh: 白宫宣布日本袭击了珍珠港。

sentences.en: 1941, a date which will live in infamy.
sentences.zh: 1941年，这是一个将永远活在耻辱中的日子。

sentences.en: By tomorrow morning, the members of Congress will have a foreport.
sentences.zh: 到明天早上，国会议员们将收到一份报告。

sentences.en: The fields of battle were far from Stanley's home.
sentences.zh: 战场离斯坦利的家很远。

sentences.en: But as he grew older, he couldn't stop thinking about the war and its implications.
sentences.zh: 但随着年龄的增长，他无法停止思考这场战争及其影响。

sentences.en: Stanley was consumed by some big questions.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利被一些重大问题所困扰。

sentences.en: Why did so many people willingly kill Jews in the Holocaust?
sentences.zh: 为什么那么多人心甘情愿地在大屠杀中杀害犹太人？

sentences.en: Was everyone who followed Nazi orders inherently evil?
sentences.zh: 所有服从纳粹命令的人本质上都是邪恶的吗？

sentences.en: Here he is in an educational film.
sentences.zh: 这是他在一部教育片中的片段。

sentences.en: How is it possible, I ask myself, that ordinary people,
sentences.zh: 我问自己，怎么可能，普通人，

sentences.en: who are courteous and decent in everyday life,
sentences.zh: 在日常生活中彬彬有礼、正派的人，

sentences.en: can act callously, inhumanely, without any limitations of conscience.
sentences.zh: 竟然能表现得如此冷酷、不人道，没有任何良心的束缚。

sentences.en: Phil Zimbardo remembers his classmate asking those same questions at James Monroe High School.
sentences.zh: 菲尔·津巴多记得他的同学在詹姆斯·门罗高中问过同样的问题。

sentences.en: As a high school student, he was worried that the Holocaust could happen again in America.
sentences.zh: 作为一名高中生，他担心大屠杀可能会在美国重演。

sentences.en: And everybody said, Stanley, that was Nazi Germany, that was then, we're not that kind of people.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说，斯坦利，那是纳粹德国，那是过去的事了，我们不是那种人。

sentences.en: And he would say, I'll bet they thought the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而他会说，我敢打赌他们当时也这么想。

sentences.en: And the bottom line, he says, how do you know how you would act unless you're in this situation?
sentences.zh: 他说，归根结底，除非你身处那种情境，否则你怎么知道你会怎么做？

sentences.en: How do you know how you would act unless you're in the situation?
sentences.zh: 除非你身处那种情境，否则你怎么知道你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Stanley's theory was that the context that people found themselves in shaped their behavior.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利的理论是，人们所处的情境塑造了他们的行为。

sentences.en: This went for Nazis, but it went for ordinary people too.
sentences.zh: 这对纳粹适用，对普通人也适用。

sentences.en: Most of us never get to find out if we will behave like Nazis
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人永远不会知道自己是否会像纳粹那样行事，

sentences.en: because most of us never find ourselves in situations where we're asked to behave like Nazis.
sentences.zh: 因为我们大多数人从未发现自己处于被要求像纳粹那样行事的情境中。

sentences.en: By the early 1960s, as a psychology professor at Yale, Stanley decided to test this idea.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代初，作为耶鲁大学的心理学教授，斯坦利决定验证这个想法。

sentences.en: Under what conditions would a person obey authority
sentences.zh: 在什么条件下，一个人会服从权威，

sentences.en: who commanded actions that went against conscience?
sentences.zh: 去执行违背良心的行为？

sentences.en: These are exactly the questions that I wanted to investigate at Yale University.
sentences.zh: 这正是我想在耶鲁大学调查的问题。

sentences.en: Stanley wanted to put volunteers in a situation
sentences.zh: 斯坦利想把志愿者置于一种情境中，

sentences.en: where they would be asked to do something that was clearly wrong.
sentences.zh: 在那里他们会被要求做一些明显错误的事情。

sentences.en: Would they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们会做吗？

sentences.en: Follow instructions?
sentences.zh: 会听从指示吗？

sentences.en: Obey orders?
sentences.zh: 会服从命令吗？

sentences.en: He came up with a scenario that was simple, ingenious, and wildly controversial.
sentences.zh: 他想出了一个简单、巧妙且极具争议的方案。

sentences.en: An experimenter wearing a lab coat invited volunteers into a room.
sentences.zh: 一名穿着实验服的实验者邀请志愿者进入一个房间。

sentences.en: The volunteers were told they were part of a study about learning and memory.
sentences.zh: 志愿者被告知他们是一项关于学习和记忆的研究的一部分。

sentences.en: Some would play the role of teacher, while others would play a student.
sentences.zh: 有些人将扮演老师的角色，而另一些人将扮演学生。

sentences.en: What you're going to hear next is a recreation of the study using voice actors.
sentences.zh: 接下来您将听到的是使用配音演员对该研究的重现。

sentences.en: The dialogue is drawn from a 1962 documentary that describes the experiment.
sentences.zh: 对话摘自1962年一部描述该实验的纪录片。

sentences.en: Before we begin, we should know that some listeners may find this section upsetting
sentences.zh: 在开始之前，我们应该知道，一些听众可能会觉得这一部分令人不安，

sentences.en: because it involves descriptions of someone inflicting pain on another person.
sentences.zh: 因为它涉及对某人向他人施加痛苦的描述。

sentences.en: Also, there are two liberties we've taken in this recreation.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们在这次重现中采取了两种自由处理方式。

sentences.en: First, in the real version of this experiment,
sentences.zh: 首先，在真实版本的实验中，

sentences.en: the student responded to the teacher's questions by silently flipping a switch.
sentences.zh: 学生通过静默地拨动开关来回应老师的问题。

sentences.en: We've given voice to those actions.
sentences.zh: 我们为这些动作配上了声音。

sentences.en: Second, we've imagined the internal monologues of some of the people in the experiment.
sentences.zh: 其次，我们想象了实验中一些人的内心独白。

sentences.en: Those inner voices sound different from the things they say aloud,
sentences.zh: 那些内心声音听起来与他们大声说出来的话不同，

sentences.en: and you'll hear them both throughout the scene.
sentences.zh: 在整个场景中，您会听到这两者。

sentences.en: So, that's the setup for the experiment.
sentences.zh: 那么，这就是实验的设置。

sentences.en: Remember, there was an experimenter and two volunteers,
sentences.zh: 记住，有一名实验者和两名志愿者，

sentences.en: one playing the role of teacher and the other playing the role of student.
sentences.zh: 一个扮演老师，另一个扮演学生。

sentences.en: The experimenter began by explaining the purpose of the memory teSt.
sentences.zh: 实验者首先解释了记忆测试的目的。

sentences.en: We want to find out just what effect different people have on each other as teachers and learners,
sentences.zh: 我们想找出不同的人作为老师和学习者对彼此有什么影响，

sentences.en: and also what effect punishment will have on learning in this situation.
sentences.zh: 以及惩罚在这种情况下对学习有什么影响。

sentences.en: The experimenter told the person playing the role of student to sit in a chair.
sentences.zh: 实验者告诉扮演学生的人坐在椅子上。

sentences.en: The experimenter strapped down the student's arms and attached an electrode to his wriSt.
sentences.zh: 实验者绑住了学生的手臂，并在他的手腕上连接了一个电极。

sentences.en: The electrode, the student was told, was connected to a shock generator.
sentences.zh: 学生被告知，电极连接着一个电击发生器。

sentences.en: Then the experimenter explained,
sentences.zh: 然后实验者解释说，

sentences.en: The teacher will read a list of word pairs to you, like these.
sentences.zh: 老师会为你读一串词对，就像这些。

sentences.en: Blue, girl, nice day, fat neck, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 蓝色、女孩、美好的一天、粗脖子，等等。

sentences.en: You are to try to remember each pair.
sentences.zh: 你要试着记住每一对。

sentences.en: For the next time through, the teacher will read only the first word or the first half of the word pair.
sentences.zh: 在下一次循环中，老师只会读第一个词或词对的前半部分。

sentences.en: The student was asked to remember the second half of the word pair.
sentences.zh: 学生被要求记住词对的后半部分。

sentences.en: The experimenter made sure to ask.
sentences.zh: 实验者特意问了一句。

sentences.en: Do you have any questions now before we go to the next room?
sentences.zh: 在去下一个房间之前，你现在有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: No, but I think I should say this.
sentences.zh: 没有，但我认为我应该说一下。

sentences.en: About two years ago, I was at the Veterans Hospital in West Haven,
sentences.zh: 大约两年前，我在西黑文的退伍军人医院，

sentences.en: and while there, they detected a heart condition.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他们检测出我患有心脏病。

sentences.en: There's nothing serious, but as long as I'm having these shocks,
sentences.zh: 没什么严重的，但只要我还在接受这些电击，

sentences.en: how strong are they?
sentences.zh: 它们有多强？

sentences.en: How dangerous are they?
sentences.zh: 它们有多危险？

sentences.en: Well, no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，并不危险。

sentences.en: Although they may be painful, they're not dangerous.
sentences.zh: 虽然可能会感到疼痛，但它们并不危险。

sentences.en: Next, the experimenter ushered the volunteer playing the role of teacher into another room.
sentences.zh: 接下来，实验人员将扮演“老师”角色的志愿者带进了另一个房间。

sentences.en: He gave him a set of instructions.
sentences.zh: 他给了他一套说明。

sentences.en: You will read each pair of words in this list once to the learner
sentences.zh: 你将把这份清单上的每一对词读给学习者听一遍

sentences.en: until you've read the entire liSt.
sentences.zh: 直到你读完整个清单。

sentences.en: Direct your voice toward the microphone
sentences.zh: 请对着麦克风说话，

sentences.en: as the rooms are only partly soundproof.
sentences.zh: 因为房间的隔音效果有限。

sentences.en: Now, if he gives the correct answer,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果他回答正确，

sentences.en: you say correct and go on to the next line.
sentences.zh: 你就说“正确”，然后继续下一行。

sentences.en: The correct answer is...
sentences.zh: 正确答案是……

sentences.en: Okay, here goes.
sentences.zh: 好的，开始了。

sentences.en: It is indicated in the right margin.
sentences.zh: 它标在右侧边栏里。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Looks easy enough.

sentences.zh: 被别人置于尴尬境地是什么感觉。

sentences.en: We think of our bosses, our partners, our co-workers,
sentences.zh: 我们会想到我们的老板、伴侣、同事，

sentences.en: and how they affect our lives and change our moods.
sentences.zh: 以及他们如何影响我们的生活和情绪。

sentences.en: We think of the aggressive driver next to us
sentences.zh: 我们会想到旁边那个咄咄逼人的司机，

sentences.en: or the other patrons at the restaurant who are so loud and obnoxious
sentences.zh: 或者餐馆里那些吵闹又讨厌的顾客，

sentences.en: that they ruin our meal.
sentences.zh: 他们毁了我们的用餐体验。

sentences.en: We feel buffeted and pushed and pulled by those around us.
sentences.zh: 我们感到被周围的人推搡和摆布。

sentences.en: The one thing we don't ask?
sentences.zh: 唯一一件我们不问的事是什么？

sentences.en: What effect do I have on other people?
sentences.zh: 我对其他人有什么影响？

sentences.en: There's been a long history of research on social influence and persuasion,
sentences.zh: 关于社会影响力和说服力的研究历史悠久，

sentences.en: so we do know a lot about how other people influence us,
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实很了解别人如何影响我们，

sentences.en: but we don't know so much about how we experience our influence of other people.
sentences.zh: 但我们不太了解我们如何体验自己对他人的影响。

sentences.en: When we are intensely focused on how the world affects us
sentences.zh: 当我们专注于世界如何影响我们，

sentences.en: and not on how we affect the world,
sentences.zh: 而不是我们如何影响世界时，

sentences.en: this can have profound consequences for both good and evil.
sentences.zh: 这可能会对善恶产生深远的影响。

sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: When Vanessa Barnes was a graduate student at Columbia University,
sentences.zh: 当凡妮莎·巴恩斯在哥伦比亚大学读研究生时，

sentences.en: she worked on a study.
sentences.zh: 她参与了一项研究。

sentences.en: Every day, she would leave her apartment in the Morningside Heights neighborhood of New York
sentences.zh: 每天，她都会离开位于纽约晨边高地的公寓，

sentences.en: and get on the subway and take the one train from 116th Street to Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 坐上地铁，搭乘1号线从116街前往宾夕法尼亚车站。

sentences.en: This is 34th Street, Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 这是34街，宾夕法尼亚车站。

sentences.en: Basically, I would just go up to random people in Penn Station,
sentences.zh: 基本上，我就是走到宾夕法尼亚车站的陌生人面前，

sentences.en: say, hey, will you fill out this questionnaire?
sentences.zh: 说，嘿，你能填一下这份问卷吗？

sentences.en: Vanessa no longer remembers what the questionnaire was about,
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎已经不记得问卷的内容是什么了，

sentences.en: but she can still recall what it felt like to make such requests of total strangers.
sentences.zh: 但她仍然记得向完全陌生的人提出这种要求是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I still have flashbacks of going down to Penn Station
sentences.zh: 是啊，我的意思是，我至今还会闪回在宾夕法尼亚车站的情景，

sentences.en: because it was so distressing.
sentences.zh: 因为那太令人痛苦了。

sentences.en: I would walk in, there'd be people kind of walking all over the place,
sentences.zh: 我走进去，到处都是走来走去的人，

sentences.en: and then there'd be people just sitting down waiting for their trains.
sentences.zh: 还有些人只是坐着等火车。

sentences.en: So I'd usually go up to the person who was sitting there waiting for their train, you know, doing whatever they do to kind of occupy their time.
sentences.zh: 所以我通常会走到那个坐着等火车的人面前，你知道，做着他们用来打发时间的事。

sentences.en: And I would say, excuse me, will you please fill out the survey?
sentences.zh: 然后我会说，打扰一下，你能填一下这份调查问卷吗？

sentences.en: It felt incredibly awkward.
sentences.zh: 感觉极其尴尬。

sentences.en: Stepping into someone's space, disturbing them, asking them to stop doing what they were doing and to do something she wanted them to do.
sentences.zh: 闯入别人的空间，打扰他们，要求他们停止正在做的事，去做她想让他们做的事。

sentences.en: As Vanessa asked for help and waited for an answer, her palms began to sweat.
sentences.zh: 当凡妮莎寻求帮助并等待回应时，她的手心开始出汗。

sentences.en: Her heart started beating faster.
sentences.zh: 她的心跳开始加速。

sentences.en: It was a really sort of palpable fear that they were going to reject me, or worse, right, say something mean.
sentences.zh: 那是一种非常明显的恐惧，怕他们会拒绝我，或者更糟，说些刻薄的话。

sentences.en: I don't even know what, but I expected them to say something terrible.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道是什么，但我预料他们会说些可怕的话。

sentences.en: Looking back on the moment now, it reminds her of another Stanley Milgram study, one that's less famous than the obedience experiment.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，这让她想起了斯坦利·米尔格拉姆的另一项研究，那项研究不如服从实验出名。

sentences.en: He had his research assistants go onto New York City subways and ask people for their seats.
sentences.zh: 他让研究助理去纽约地铁上，要求人们让座。

sentences.en: Many of his students couldn't complete the task.
sentences.zh: 他的许多学生无法完成这项任务。

sentences.en: His students started coming back to him saying, I can't do this.
sentences.zh: 他的学生回来对他说，我做不到。

sentences.en: This is just so upsetting.
sentences.zh: 这太让人难受了。

sentences.en: This is the most, you know, distressing thing you've ever asked me to do.
sentences.zh: 这是你让我做过的最令人痛苦的事情。

sentences.en: And he was like, you guys are being babies.
sentences.zh: 而他说，你们太孩子气了。

sentences.en: I don't understand why this is so upsetting.
sentences.zh: 我不明白这有什么好难受的。

sentences.en: And so, to prove his students wrong, the famous researcher set out for the subway himself.
sentences.zh: 于是，为了证明学生们错了，这位著名的研究员亲自去了地铁。

sentences.en: He would do what his students couldn't.
sentences.zh: 他要去做学生们做不到的事。

sentences.en: Walk up to strangers and ask them for their seats.
sentences.zh: 走到陌生人面前，要求他们让座。

sentences.en: He found the experience so much more distressing than he expected it to be,
sentences.zh: 他发现这段经历比他预想的要痛苦得多，

sentences.en: and all of a sudden he understood why they had been complaining so much.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他明白了为什么他们抱怨得那么厉害。

sentences.en: Why is it so hard to make such requests?
sentences.zh: 为什么提出这样的要求这么难？

sentences.en: Well, one obvious explanation is that we know that people will reject us,
sentences.zh: 嗯，一个显而易见的解释是，我们知道人们会拒绝我们，

sentences.en: and that rejection is painful.
sentences.zh: 而那种拒绝是痛苦的。

sentences.en: Vanessa remembers being hugely relieved when she was done giving out questionnaires at Penn Station
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎记得在宾夕法尼亚车站发完问卷后，她感到如释重负，

sentences.en: and could head back to her lab at Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 可以回到哥伦比亚大学的实验室了。

sentences.en: Once there, she and her professor, Frank Flynn, analyzed the responses to the questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 到了那里，她和她的教授弗兰克·弗林分析了问卷的回复。

sentences.en: They noticed something intriguing.
sentences.zh: 他们注意到了一些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: Frank was like, I can't believe how many people are actually saying yes to you.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说，我简直不敢相信竟然有这么多人答应你。

sentences.en: Total strangers, disrupted from reading their newspaper or eating a sandwich or watching the crowds of people in the busy station,
sentences.zh: 完全陌生的人，在忙碌的车站里，被从看报纸、吃三明治或看人群中打断，

sentences.en: they were like, sure, I'll respond to your questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 他们当时就说，没问题，我会回答你的问卷。

sentences.en: We were really surprised by how many people were agreeing in New York Penn Station to do this survey.
sentences.zh: 我们在纽约宾夕法尼亚车站进行这项调查时，有多少人愿意配合，这让我们感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: What began as a simple observation turned into something much more important, an insight about our minds.
sentences.zh: 起初只是一个简单的观察，后来却演变成了一件意义重大的事情，让我们对自己的思维有了新的洞察。

sentences.en: Here's the chain of thought that led to the discovery.
sentences.zh: 以下是促成这一发现的思维链条。

sentences.en: The reason Frank and Vanessa were surprised that so many people said yes is because they expected people to say no.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和凡妮莎之所以对这么多人答应感到惊讶，是因为他们预料到人们会拒绝。

sentences.en: If lots of people said yes, that meant that Vanessa's fears about rejection were misplaced.
sentences.zh: 如果很多人都答应了，那就意味着凡妮莎对被拒绝的恐惧是多余的。

sentences.en: her perception of the influence she actually had on other people was wrong.
sentences.zh: 她对自己实际上对他人的影响力有着错误的认知。

sentences.en: Like most of us, Vanessa had long felt that others had a big effect on her.
sentences.zh: 和我们大多数人一样，凡妮莎长期以来一直觉得别人对她有很大的影响。

sentences.en: As she gazed at the data, she realized that she had a big effect on other people.
sentences.zh: 当她凝视着这些数据时，她意识到自己对别人也有很大的影响。

sentences.en: If she was blind to this power, what consequences could it have on her behavior?
sentences.zh: 如果她对这种力量视而不见，这会对她的行为产生什么后果呢？

sentences.en: As researchers, the first thing that Vanessa and Frank decided to do
sentences.zh: 作为研究人员，凡妮莎和弗兰克决定做的第一件事

sentences.en: was test if that personal experience was generalizable.
sentences.zh: 就是测试这种个人经历是否具有普遍性。

sentences.en: We decided to bring participants into the lab
sentences.zh: 我们决定把参与者带到实验室里，

sentences.en: and have them do basically what I had done on those number of days.
sentences.zh: 让他们做我那几天所做的事情。

sentences.en: So we brought them into the lab.
sentences.zh: 于是我们把他们带到了实验室。

sentences.en: We said, hey, we're going to have you go out and ask people to,
sentences.zh: 我们说，嘿，我们要让你出去请人，

sentences.en: as our first step, fill out a survey, just like I had done.
sentences.zh: 第一步，填一份问卷，就像我做的那样。

sentences.en: And how many people do you think are going to say yes to you?
sentences.zh: 你觉得会有多少人答应你？

sentences.en: We made them estimate how many people they thought would agree,
sentences.zh: 我们让他们预估会有多少人同意，

sentences.en: go out and actually ask people.
sentences.zh: 然后出去真正地去询问别人。

sentences.en: And what we found was that they really underestimated
sentences.zh: 我们发现，他们确实低估了

sentences.en: of the number of people who had agreed to that requeSt.
sentences.zh: 答应这一请求的人数。

sentences.en: So it wasn't just Vanessa and Frank.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是凡妮莎和弗兰克的问题。

sentences.en: People in general seemed to have a poor assessment of their power over others.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍对自己对他人的影响力评估不足。

sentences.en: People thought that others would find it easy to turn down their requests.
sentences.zh: 人们认为别人会很容易拒绝他们的请求。

sentences.en: Vanessa connected the seeming blind spot in our thinking to Stanley Milgram's famous
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎将我们思维中这种看似盲点的地方与斯坦利·米尔格拉姆著名的

sentences.en: obedience study.
sentences.zh: 服从研究联系了起来。

sentences.en: She realized this might be why everyone always saw the experiment from the perspective of
sentences.zh: 她意识到，这可能就是为什么每个人总是从

sentences.en: of volunteers asked to administer shocks, the people being influenced.
sentences.zh: 被要求施加电击的志愿者，也就是受影响者的角度来看待这个实验的原因。

sentences.en: No one saw the experiment
sentences.zh: 没有人从

sentences.en: from the point of view of the experimenter, the person exercising influence.
sentences.zh: 实验者，也就是施加影响的人的角度来看待这个实验。

sentences.en: We don't ask,
sentences.zh: 我们不会问，

sentences.en: was it hard for him to issue those crazy instructions because we don't identify with
sentences.zh: 他发布那些疯狂的指令是否感到困难，因为我们不会代入

sentences.en: people exercising such influence?
sentences.zh: 那些施加这种影响力的人？

sentences.en: We think that kind of person must be very different from us
sentences.zh: 我们认为那种人一定和我们非常不同，

sentences.en: because we don't feel we have such power.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不觉得我们有那样的力量。

sentences.en: Was he surprised to see these people going along
sentences.zh: 他看到这些人顺从

sentences.en: with this crazy request he was making of them?
sentences.zh: 他提出的疯狂要求时，他感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: So it's interesting when people think
sentences.zh: 所以，当人们思考

sentences.en: about the Stanley Milgram study,
sentences.zh: 斯坦利·米尔格拉姆的研究时，这很有趣，

sentences.en: and I think this is true for myself as well,
sentences.zh: 我想我自己也是这样，

sentences.en: I always imagine myself being in the role
sentences.zh: 我总是想象自己处于

sentences.en: of the volunteer in the experiment,
sentences.zh: 实验中志愿者的角色，

sentences.en: hearing the instructions from the experimenter saying,
sentences.zh: 听到实验者发出的指令说，

sentences.en: you must shock this other person.
sentences.zh: 你必须电击另一个人。

sentences.en: I never put myself in the shoes of the experimenter.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有设身处地地站在实验者的角度去想。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that was something that we started to wonder about.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们开始思考的问题。

sentences.en: So we so often sort of simulate, if I was in that Milgram shock experiment, what would
sentences.zh: 我们经常会模拟，如果我身处那个米尔格拉姆电击实验中，我会

sentences.en: I do if I was the study participant, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我是研究参与者，我会怎么做，对吧？

sentences.en: Would I actually stand up and go against these directives and say no?
sentences.zh: 我会站出来反抗这些指令并说不吗？

sentences.en: But we kind of flipped that idea on its head.
sentences.zh: 但我们把这个想法颠倒过来了。

sentences.en: Vanessa went back to her experience at Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎回到了她在宾夕法尼亚车站的经历。

sentences.en: It felt difficult because she had seen the interaction only from the point of view of
sentences.zh: 这感觉很困难，因为她只从自己的角度看待这次互动，

sentences.en: her own insecurities.
sentences.zh: 带着她自己的不安全感。

sentences.en: She hadn't seen the encounters through the point of view of the people she was asking for help.
sentences.zh: 她没有从她寻求帮助的人的角度来看待这些接触。

sentences.en: From their perspective, an anxious young woman was asking for something trivial.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，一个焦虑的年轻女子在请求一件琐事。

sentences.en: They had to weigh whether to put aside what they were doing and help her for a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 他们必须权衡是否要放下手头的工作，帮她几分钟。

sentences.en: If they said no, it could make them look like jerks.
sentences.zh: 如果他们拒绝，可能会显得他们很混蛋。

sentences.en: It's this really interesting phenomenon where you have these two people interacting with one another
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的现象，你有这两个人正在互动，

sentences.en: and they're both so focused on their own personal anxieties and insecurities and concerns with
sentences.zh: 他们都太专注于自己的个人焦虑、不安全感和对

sentences.en: embarrassment that they don't realize that the other person is feeling that way, too.
sentences.zh: 尴尬的担忧，以至于他们没有意识到对方也有同样的感受。

sentences.en: So it's
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个

sentences.en: this really interesting situation where being so inwardly focused on your own anxieties makes it
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的情况，因为过于关注自己的焦虑，使得

sentences.en: so difficult for you to recognize what the situation really is for itself.
sentences.zh: 你很难认清情况的本质。

sentences.en: People in these
sentences.zh: 处于这些

sentences.en: encounters experience what psychologists call an egocentric bias.
sentences.zh: 接触中的人们会经历心理学家所说的自我中心偏见。

sentences.en: They are so consumed with
sentences.zh: 他们太沉浸于

sentences.en: their own perceptions that they fail to see what the interaction feels like for the other person.
sentences.zh: 自己的感知，以至于无法看到对方对这次互动的感受。

sentences.en: It's absolutely true that many of us are influenced by situations that many of us will do things
sentences.zh: 我们许多人确实会受到情境的影响，我们许多人会做某些事

sentences.en: because the situation prompts it.
sentences.zh: 是因为情境促使我们这样做。

sentences.en: But there is another problem too, and it might be a deeper
sentences.zh: 但还有一个问题，而且这可能是一个更深层的

sentences.en: problem.
sentences.zh: 问题。

sentences.en: The people who put us in those situations, it's not like they are all-powerful gods.
sentences.zh: 那些把我们置于这些情境中的人，他们并不是全能的神。

sentences.en: They are humans just like us, and they may not realize the extent of the power they have over us.
sentences.zh: 他们和我们一样是普通人，他们可能没有意识到他们对我们有多大的影响力。

sentences.en: In fact, they may be thinking, I'm sure this person is going to turn down my requeSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们可能在想，我敢肯定这个人会拒绝我的请求。

sentences.en: They might assume, falsely, that it's easy to refuse instructions.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会错误地认为，拒绝指令很容易。

sentences.en: Vanessa realized that this bias could have all sorts of important consequences.
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎意识到这种偏见可能会产生各种重要的后果。

sentences.en: So what we started looking at about over a decade now ago, we started to look at whether
sentences.zh: 所以我们大约在十多年前开始研究，我们开始观察我们是否

sentences.en: we recognize when we're the ones who are influencing someone else.
sentences.zh: 能意识到自己正在影响别人。

sentences.en: When we recognize that someone else, for example, can't say no to something, that we've asked them.
sentences.zh: 当我们意识到别人，例如，无法拒绝我们提出的某件事时。

sentences.en: Vanessa is now a psychologist at Cornell University.
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎现在是康奈尔大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: She's the author of the forthcoming book, You Have More Influence Than You Think.
sentences.zh: 她是即将出版的《你的影响力比你想象的更大》一书的作者。

sentences.en: In a series of experiments, she has demonstrated how people are often oblivious to the power that they have over others.
sentences.zh: 在一系列实验中，她证明了人们往往对自己对他人的影响力一无所知。

sentences.en: In one study, she asked volunteers, mostly college students, to make a simple requeSt.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，她要求志愿者（主要是大学生）提出一个简单的请求。

sentences.en: We brought people into the lab, and we told them,
sentences.zh: 我们把人们带到实验室，告诉他们，

sentences.en: you're going to go out into campus and ask people to borrow their phones.
sentences.zh: 你要去校园里请人借用他们的手机。

sentences.en: She walked them through how to approach someone
sentences.zh: 她指导他们如何接近某人，

sentences.en: and gave them instructions for what to do
sentences.zh: 并告诉他们一旦人们同意让他们使用手机后该怎么做。

sentences.en: once people agreed to let them use their phones.
sentences.zh: 他们会打回实验室告诉我们，

sentences.en: They would call us back at the lab and say,
sentences.zh: 我拿到了这个人的手机，我现在在这个位置。

sentences.en: I have this person's phone, this is where I'm located.
sentences.zh: 我们会记录下来，然后他们会继续去问下一个人。

sentences.en: We'd mark it down, and then they'd go on and ask somebody else.
sentences.zh: 在志愿者出去开始研究之前，

sentences.en: Before the volunteers went out to begin the study,
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎问了他们一个问题。

sentences.en: Vanessa asked them a question.

sentences.en: Instead of seeing the experiment from the point of view of the passers-by
sentences.zh: 而是从研究助理的角度来看这个实验。

sentences.en: and asking myself whether I would be similarly influenced,
sentences.zh: 他们是否预料到会有这么多人加入他们，一起看着虚无的天空？

sentences.en: I looked at the experiment from the point of view of the research assistants.
sentences.zh: 我们在这一集中看到，我们每个人作为个体，都有巨大的力量来塑造他人的行为。

sentences.en: Did they expect so many people to join them in looking at nothing?
sentences.zh: 如果我们每个人都有这种隐藏的力量，那么作为一个群体、社区或部落，我们将拥有更大的影响力。

sentences.en: We've seen throughout this episode how all of us as individuals have great power to shape how others behave.
sentences.zh: 我们共同施加的力量，对于任何个人来说几乎都是无法抗拒的。

sentences.en: If each of us has this hidden power, then collectively, as groups, as communities, as tribes, we are going to have even more influence.
sentences.zh: 这可以解释好的方面，比如维系社区的社会规范。

sentences.en: The force we collectively exert can be nearly impossible for any one person to overcome.
sentences.zh: 但它也可能导致可怕的事情。

sentences.en: This can explain good things, like the social norms that hold communities together.
sentences.zh: 当我们成为暴民的一部分时，其后果可能是极其可怕的。

sentences.en: But it can also lead to terrible things.
